dialogue.content: （おはようございます。今日はよろしくお願いします。）
dialogue.English: (Good morning. I'm looking forward to our session today.)

dialogue.content: おはようございます。こちらこそよろしくお願いします
dialogue.English: Good morning. Likewise, thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: （時間前で（時間前ですが、定時からスタートしますか？）
dialogue.English: (We're a little early. Shall we wait until the scheduled time to begin?)

dialogue.content: はい定時でお願いします！
dialogue.English: Yes, at the scheduled time would be great!

dialogue.content: （承知しました。）
dialogue.English: (Understood.)

dialogue.content: おはようございます。相談員です。まず初めによろしかったら年齢、性別、相談内容についてお聞かせ下さい。
dialogue.English: Good morning. I'm your counselor. To begin, if you're comfortable, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 35歳女性部下の事で悩んでいます
dialogue.English: I'm a 35-year-old woman, and I'm having trouble with a subordinate.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、お悩みなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so that's what's troubling you.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 具体的には部下の方のどのようなことでお悩みなんでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Could you tell me more specifically what kind of trouble you're having with your subordinate?

dialogue.content: 私はアパレルの店長をしているのですが副店長の子が仕事レベルが低すぎて困っています
dialogue.English: I'm the manager of an apparel store, and my assistant manager's work performance is so poor that it's causing problems.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、それはお困りなんでしょうね。
dialogue.English: I see, that must be very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: はい、パートさんアルバイトさんのほうがずっとレベルが高いです
dialogue.English: Yes, the part-time staff and hourly workers are much more capable.

dialogue.content: なるほど。お仕事のレベルがというお話しですが、実際どのようなことが起きていらっしゃるのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I understand. You mentioned her performance level. What kinds of things have been happening specifically?

dialogue.content: 指示したことができない、もしくは中途半端。他の売場の子とおしゃべりしていて、自分の売場にいないなどです。私が不在の時は副店長がいつもいないので探しているそうです
dialogue.English: She can't follow instructions, or she leaves things half-done. She's often chatting with staff from other departments and isn't at her post. When I'm not there, I'm told they're always looking for her because she's nowhere to be found.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、それは困ったもんですね。貴方がそう思われるのも無理もないですよね。
dialogue.English: I see, that's quite a predicament. It's completely understandable that you feel that way.

dialogue.content: はい、怒ってもぜんぜん改善されません
dialogue.English: Yes, and scolding her doesn't lead to any improvement.

dialogue.content: そうなんですか、店長という貴方の立場からも頭の痛いことですね。
dialogue.English: I see. From your position as store manager, that must be a real headache.

dialogue.content: はい、なんか自分はちゃんと仕事しているみたいに思っていて自覚がないみたいです
dialogue.English: Yes. She seems to think she’s doing her job properly and has no self-awareness.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、どうしてそういう勤務態度の方が、副店長になられたんですかね？
dialogue.English: I see. I wonder how someone with that kind of work attitude became the assistant manager.

dialogue.content: その方とのお仕事は、長いんですか？
dialogue.English: Have you been working with her for a long time?

dialogue.content: その子は、人当たりが良くて前任の店長が男性の方で、よく飲み会とかで一緒に飲みにいったりしていたのでプライベートで仲が良かったんです。たまたまパートから準社員になれる時期があって、準社員にならないかって声かけれて準社員へそれからトントン拍子に副店長までなりました。運が良かったんです。私だったら絶対推薦しないんですけどね
dialogue.English: She has a friendly personality, and the previous manager, who was a man, was good friends with her privately. They often went out drinking together. It just so happened there was an opportunity to move from part-time to associate staff, and he suggested it to her. After that, she was promoted to assistant manager in no time. She was just lucky. I would never have recommended her.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね、そういう状況で副店長になられたんですね。それは納得いかないですよね。
dialogue.English: I see—that’s how she became assistant manager in those circumstances. It’s understandable that that doesn’t sit right with you.

dialogue.content: 私もそうですが、パートさんたちもいつも腹立てています
dialogue.English: It's not just me; the part-time staff are always angry about it too.

dialogue.content: そうでしょうね、前任の店長さんに責任取ってもらいたいくらいですね。
dialogue.English: I can imagine. It makes you want to hold the previous manager responsible, doesn't it?

dialogue.content: こういう状態は、長いんですか？
dialogue.English: Has this situation been going on for a long time?

dialogue.content: 詳しく言うと前々任の店長なんですけどね。前任の店長も男性だったのですが、副店長の事は聞いていたんです。でもこんなに最悪とは思いませんでした。私が2年前に着任してからずっとですけど多分５年以上は成長ないままだと思います
dialogue.English: To be precise, it was the manager before the last one. The most recent manager was also a man, and I had heard about the assistant manager, but I never thought it would be this bad. It's been like this ever since I took the position two years ago, but I think she's been stagnant for probably more than five years.

dialogue.content: なるほどそうだったのですね、長い間お悩みなんですね。そんな中でも貴方は、仕事を続けられていらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so you've been struggling with this for a long time. And yet, despite all that, you've continued to do your job.

dialogue.content: この件は、会社の上司の方とかにご相談されましたか？大分きつい状況なので。
dialogue.English: Have you discussed this matter with your superiors at the company? It sounds like a very difficult situation.

dialogue.content: そうですね、変えてほしい事はいいましたけど、準社員なので転勤できる店がないのが現状です。正社員だったら県外とか転勤あるのですが・・・
dialogue.English: Yes, I told them I wanted her moved, but as an associate employee, there are currently no other stores she can be transferred to. If she were a full-time employee, she could be transferred out of the prefecture, but...

dialogue.content: といあえず着任したときの、あまりの出来なさに初日から怒りまくっていました。パートさんからはスッキリしたって喜ばれました。でも副店長はその時はよく怒る店長が来たとしか思ってなかったみたいで１年後くらいでやっと自分は人より仕事ができないと自覚するようになってはきました
dialogue.English: When I first started, I was so shocked by her incompetence that I was furious from day one. The part-time staff were pleased, saying it was a relief. But at the time, the assistant manager just thought a manager who gets angry a lot had arrived. It took about a year for her to finally start realizing that she's not as capable as others.

dialogue.content: そうだったのですね、貴方は色々努力されてこられたんですね。それはやりきれない思いもおありですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. You've made a lot of effort to deal with this. You must feel so frustrated.

dialogue.content: はい、仕事が一緒でなけれな気さくで良い子なんですけど、仕事となると、適当過ぎて給料泥棒です
dialogue.English: Yes. If we weren't working together, she's actually a friendly, nice person. But when it comes to work, she's so careless it feels like she's stealing her salary.

dialogue.content: （すいません、通信状態が悪くデータが送れません）
dialogue.English: (I'm sorry, the connection is poor and I can't send my message.)

dialogue.content: （気にしないで下さい。気長に待ってます！）
dialogue.English: (Don't worry about it. I'll wait patiently!)

dialogue.content: 貴方ご自身の体は大丈夫ですか？睡眠とか食事はちゃんと摂られていらっしゃいますか？
dialogue.English: How are you doing physically? Are you sleeping and eating properly?

dialogue.content: そこなんですよね・・・。食欲はあるのですが、腹が立ちすぎて考えると夜寝れない時があります。ああ言えば良かったとか考えてしまって・・・
dialogue.English: That’s the thing... I have an appetite, but I sometimes can’t sleep at night because I get so angry thinking about it. I keep replaying what I should have said...

dialogue.content: なるほど、それはお辛いですよね。
dialogue.English: I understand. That must be very hard on you.

dialogue.content: 私なりに考えたのですが興味がある事はすごい知識が高いんです。例えば好きなお店の名前とか曲だったりとか・・・。でも仕事は出来る仕事しかしません。
dialogue.English: From what I've observed, she has impressive knowledge about things she's interested in, like her favorite stores or songs... But at work, she only does what she can already handle.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、いいところもおありなんですね。色々お話伺って、貴方は部下の副店長の方のことで悩んでいらっしゃる。夜寝られないとこもある。
dialogue.English: I see, so she does have her good points. From what you've told me, you're troubled by your assistant manager, and it's even causing you to lose sleep.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お話しされて、今後どんな風になったらいいなと思われますか？
dialogue.English: Now that you've had a chance to talk about it, what would you like to see happen in the future?

dialogue.content: とりあえず、仕事の邪魔をしないでほしいです。副店長が不在の時でも昨日仕事してないなってわかるし、私が出勤するとパートさんからまず副店長の愚痴をききます。責任感がないので成長できないから責任感をもって仕事をしてくれれば別に結果が悪くても私はここまで怒ったりしないんですけど
dialogue.English: For a start, I just want her to stop interfering with the work. Even when she's been away, I can tell she didn't do her job the day before. And when I come to work, the first thing I hear from the part-timers is complaints about her. She can't grow because she has no sense of responsibility. If she would just take her job seriously, I wouldn't get this angry, even if the results aren't perfect.

dialogue.content: なるほど、では貴方のお仕事の邪魔をされないようにするには、どんな方法が考えらますかね？
dialogue.English: I see. So, what methods can we think of to prevent her from disrupting your work?

dialogue.content: 今まで強くいってきてなおらないので、性格上無理ですよね・・・。少しは仕事も覚えてきてはいるので、気長に言い続けるしかないんですかね？
dialogue.English: I’ve been very firm with her, but it hasn’t changed, so it’s probably impossible given her personality... She has learned the job a little bit, so maybe I just have to be patient and keep telling her?

dialogue.content: そうなのかもしれないですね。ではご一緒に考えていきたいと思いますが、いかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: That may be the case. If it’s alright with you, shall we think this through together?

dialogue.content: お願いします
dialogue.English: Yes, please.

dialogue.content: まず貴方の睡眠が取れないのが心配です。お風呂にゆっくり浸かったり、アロマを焚かれたり、好きな音楽を聴かれたりと、ご自分をリラックスされてはと思いますが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: First, I’m concerned about your lack of sleep. How about taking time to relax—soaking in a warm bath, using some aromatherapy, or listening to music you like—to help yourself unwind?

dialogue.content: そうですね、リラックスして寝る時は考えないように寝れたらいいと思います
dialogue.English: You're right. It would be good if I could relax and sleep without thinking about it.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、是非やってみてください。
dialogue.English: Exactly. Please give it a try.

dialogue.content: はい、やってみます
dialogue.English: Yes, I'll try it.

dialogue.content: 副店長の方については、貴方の指導で少しづつ変わられているようにも見受けます。このまま指導を続けらるのもひとつと考えます。また、仕事は仕事なので、業務怠慢であれば、辞めていただくのも視野に入れられてと思いますが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: Regarding the assistant manager, it sounds like your guidance is leading to gradual change. Continuing your coaching is one option. Also, work is work; if it amounts to neglect of duty, it may be worth considering asking her to leave. What do you think?

dialogue.content: はい、そういうことは言っています。とりあえず評価はずっと悪いので、ボーナス査定にも引っかかるので、努力するようには言っています
dialogue.English: Yes, I have told her things like that. For now, her performance reviews are consistently bad, which affects her bonus assessment, so I've told her she needs to make an effort.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、貴方も行動されていらっしゃるのですね。是非それを継続されてはと思います。
dialogue.English: I see—you’re already taking action. I encourage you to continue.

dialogue.content: 色々お話しされて、今はどのようなお気持ちですか？
dialogue.English: Having talked this through, how are you feeling now?

dialogue.content: とりあえずスッキリしました。あまりパートさんとかには愚痴れなく聞くばっかりだったので・・・。
dialogue.English: For the time being, I feel relieved. I couldn’t really vent to the part-time staff—I was always just listening to them.

dialogue.content: そうですか、それは良かったです。貴方なら大丈夫。応援しています。頑張って下さい。
dialogue.English: I see, I'm glad to hear that. I believe you can handle this. I'm rooting for you. Keep up the good work.

dialogue.content: はいありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Yes, thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 今日はこちらにお起こしいただきありがとうございます。また続きを聞かせて下さい。
dialogue.English: Thank you for coming in today. Please let me know how things go.

dialogue.content: はい、わかりました！
dialogue.English: Yes, I will!

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました。大変勉強になりました。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you very much. This was a great learning experience.)

dialogue.content: （こちらこそありがとうございました。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you as well.)
